searchText: As a procedural matter: https://forkcast.org/upgrade/glamsterdam/ doesn't contain EIP-8071 but https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-7773#proposed-for-inclusion does have it. Presumably Forkcast is delayed, but EIP-7773 is canonical? Question about EIP-8062: forkcast says it "Improves fairness between legacy 0x01 and compounding 0x02 validators". What does that even mean? What does "Aligns CL withdrawals with EL resource usage." mean? cc <@917367578966523934> And in particular, to the extent it "Incentivizes operators to consolidate for the benefit of the network", it seems like that's in some tension with the idea of "improving fairness", based on the usual definitions I see used of fairness. It's explicitly biasing outcomes. Good, bad, worthwhile, not worthwhile, that's not really about "fairness", it's about engineering incentives For EIP-8061: "while preserving a long weak-subjectivity period and existing security assumptions." is just, straightforwardly, not consistent with the EIP. https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-8061#weak-subjectivity-period notes it decreases the WSP from about 16 days to somewhere between 7-10 days Every withdrawal comes with data in the block + a state diff on the EL. This requires loading the account of the wd recipient from disk, write to it, and update the post state root. Right now the EL charges nothing for that, although withdrawals do consume EL resources. It's cleaner to have the CL deduct that fee already such that the EL doesn't need to care about it or change anything in it's wd-processing logic. It's possible to just deduct e.g. the fee for creating a new account on the EL but less clean than doing it at the CL. Where is the sentence about EIP-8061 from? It's not in the EIP, and the EIP does clearly acknowledge that it's reducing the weak subjectivity period, as early as in the abstract re: 8061, I am happy to take in any implementation feedback and evolve towards a version that best balances not adding extra load to the fork with the main objectives, i.e. increasing exit and consolidation churn https://forkcast.org/upgrade/glamsterdam/ currently the forkcast summary is misleading I brought this up with <@119818938845495298> already, it should be added on forkcast soon so I can have a proper graphic for our blog post I'll make a PR to fix it in a bit gm gm ! excerpts.author: tersec
excerpts.content: For EIP-8061: "while preserving a long weak-subjectivity period and existing security assumptions." is just, straightforwardly, not consistent with the EIP. https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-8061#weak-subjectivity-period notes it decreases the WSP from about 16 days to somewhere between 7-10 days

excerpts.author: nero_eth
excerpts.content: Every withdrawal comes with data in the block + a state diff on the EL. This requires loading the account of the wd recipient from disk, write to it, and update the post state root. Right now the EL charges nothing for that, although withdrawals do consume EL resources.

excerpts.author: nero_eth
excerpts.content: It's cleaner to have the CL deduct that fee already such that the EL doesn't need to care about it or change anything in it's wd-processing logic. It's possible to just deduct e.g. the fee for creating a new account on the EL but less clean than doing it at the CL.
